descriptionChirho: Corrective discipline or chastening, especially by God as a father disciplines a child (Heb 12:5-8, 11); also the punishment or reproof aspect of moral training. The emphasis falls on correction through suffering or rebuke. Hindi 'ताड़ना' (chastisement), Arabic 'تَأْدِيب' (disciplining), Korean '징계' (disciplinary action), Swahili 'adhabu' (punishment) all point toward the corrective-punitive end of the semantic spectrum. This sense appears in Hebrews 12 and Ephesians 6:4 where the context explicitly discusses fatherly correction and its painful but fruit-bearing nature.

The formative aspect of rearing — training, education, and moral instruction that shapes character over time, as in 2 Timothy 3:16 where Scripture is useful for 'training in righteousness.' Spanish 'instrucción' (instruction), Hindi 'शिकशित करन' (to educate/train), Korean '훈련을 위해' (for the purpose of training), Swahili 'kuadibisha' (to instruct/train) and Arabic 'التَّأْديبِ' all reflect the pedagogical-formative nuance rather than punitive correction. While overlapping with sense 1, this sense foregrounds the constructive-educational dimension of paideia.
